title: How do we find the two centres of an eye's arcs?
description: A line segment X Y holds the two corners of an eye. Equal arcs from X and from Y meet above and below the segment, and those two meeting points become the centres of the eye's arcs. Keeko's doubt, a smaller arc from Y, is tested and struck out.
teaching_notes: One idea: a centre for an even eye must be the same distance from both corners, and equal arcs from X and Y meet exactly at such a place. Watch for students who change the radius between X and Y.

source: XY is a line segment. Using only a ruler and a compass, find
video_script.why: The child can draw an arc but has not used two equal arcs from two points to fix a point exactly.
video_script.substitution: A centre for an even eye must be the same distance from both corners, and equal arcs from X and Y meet exactly at such a place.
video_script.anchor: The corners X and Y of an eye on a line segment: find the two centres eigh and B of the eye's arcs.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws a big arc from X and a smaller arc from Y. They meet at a point nearer Y than X, so an arc from there cannot pass through both corners.
video_script.payoff_line: The centres are where equal arcs from X and Y meet

final_answer.value: A and B are the meeting points of equal arcs from X and Y; the arc centred at A is the lower arc and the arc centred at B is the upper arc
final_answer.spoken: the centres are where equal arcs from X and Y meet, above and below X Y

never_show: the finished eye before the last step
maths_rules: Same radius r from X and from Y, with r more than half of XY, so that the arcs meet; arcs above and below XY.
The meeting point above XY is A, the one below is B; AX = AY = BX = BY = r.
The arc with centre A and radius AX, from X to Y, is the lower arc; the arc with centre B and the same radius is the upper arc.
Slip: radii r from X and s from Y with s smaller than r give a point P with PX = r and PY = s, so PX is not equal to PY and no arc from P passes through both X and Y.
video_script.design: One idea: equal arcs from both corners fix each centre. The segment X Y stays the whole video. Keeko's doubt is a smaller arc from Y.
